turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files describing perovskite solar cells as
complete devices — `substrate` (glass + transparent electrode), `etl`
(electron-transport layer stack), `htl` (hole-transport layer stack),
`backcontact` (metal / carbon back electrode), `deposition` (absorber
deposition procedure; `>>` separates steps). Every candidate below uses the
same MAPbI3 absorber in the same p-i-n (inverted) architecture; they differ
only in the remaining columns. Each row is a device CONFIGURATION whose
efficiency is the median over at least 3 independently fabricated cells, so
it is a reproducible recipe rather than a single champion cell:
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_train.csv: 300 configurations with the measured power
    conversion efficiency (%).
  - b3_pvk_stack_pin_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE configurations whose power
    conversion efficiency (%) was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same device columns.

Using the training data, select the 5 candidates with the HIGHEST power
conversion efficiency (%).

Reason from the device physics — band alignment and selectivity of the
transport layers, interface recombination, contact chemistry and the film
quality the process is likely to give — then end your answer with an
explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902,
c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
## Recommended top five

**I would select c030, c038, c097, c044, and c088, in that order.** This is a physics-informed prediction anchored to closely related training configurations—not a claim that the unmeasured efficiencies are known. The ordering of the last three is particularly close.

In this inverted architecture, the strongest candidates combine a selective hole contact, a fullerene-based electron contact, and interface treatments that can reduce recombination without introducing excessive resistance. I prioritize evidence from complete, similar devices over assuming that any one material is universally beneficial.

| Rank | Candidate | Training evidence and device-physics rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | **c030** | The training device with **PTAA \| PMMA / PCBM-60 \| Bphen / Al**, on the same ITO substrate and using spin-coating, reaches **19.48%**. c030 preserves that combination and adds IDTT2FPDI ahead of PCBM. PTAA provides hole selectivity; sufficiently thin PMMA can suppress interfacial recombination while permitting hole extraction. PCBM/Bphen supports electron collection and separates the absorber from Al. The added electron-accepting interlayer could improve interfacial coverage or extraction, although its benefit is not directly established by the training data. |
| **2** | **c038** | The closest distinctive hole-contact analogue—**Au-np \| NiO-c / PCBM-60 / Ag** on FTO—records **20.0%**. c038 retains that hole-contact structure and adds PEI at the electron-contact side. NiO offers hole selectivity and electron blocking; the Au nanoparticles may improve the effective contact or optical response, depending on their morphology. PEI can modify the cathode-side interface dipole and facilitate extraction. This is a high-upside choice, but transferring the Au-nanoparticle benefit across substrate and contact changes is an important uncertainty. |
| **3** | **c097** | This closely matches the **18.49%** training configuration with **ITCPTC-Th \| C60 \| BCP / P3CT-Na / Ag**, replacing only ITCPTC-Th with ITCPTC-Se. It retains the selective polymer hole contact, fullerene electron-transport layer, and BCP cathode buffer. The sulfur-to-selenium substitution may alter packing and energy levels; I do not assume it must improve efficiency, but this is a strong near-neighbour to an already high-performing complete device. |
| **4** | **c044** | **PTAA / PCBM-60 \| BCP / Cu** is supported by several strong neighbours: the corresponding Ag-contact recipe gives **17.345%**, while **PTAA / PCBM-60 \| C60 \| BCP / Cu** gives **18.85%**. PTAA and PCBM provide complementary carrier selectivity, and BCP helps manage the electron-contact interface. Removing the additional C60 layer could reduce coverage or contact protection, so I place it slightly below the strongest multilayer analogue. |
| **5** | **c088** | The **PTAA / C60 \| BCP / Cu** combination reaches **18.62%** with sequential spin-coating and **19.085%** with slot-die coating in training. Doctor-bladed PTAA/C60/BCP devices with Ag also reach **16.9%**, supporting compatibility with a coating process. Willow glass retains a glass/ITO electrode platform rather than introducing a polymer substrate. Its main uncertainty is absorber crystallization and coverage under doctor blading, not an obviously unfavorable transport-layer combination. |

I would **not** extrapolate the training set’s **24.8% PCBM-60/TmPyPB** result to every candidate containing an unfamiliar electron-contact modifier: molecular energy levels, interfacial dipoles, coverage, and conductivity are too specific for that inference.

**Final: c030, c038, c097, c044, c088**
